title: What Is An Assumable Mortgage?
h2: What Does The Assumable Clause Look Like?

faqs.a: An assumable mortgage is one where the lender includes a clause allowing a third party, typically the homebuyer, to take over the existing mortgage. If the mortgage is not assumable, the clause will clearly state so.

faqs.q: What does an assumable clause look like?
faqs.a: A typical assumable clause may read: 'If all or any part of the property is sold or transferred without the lender’s prior consent, the lender may require immediate payment in full of the loan.' This means the mortgage may be assumed if the lender is notified and consents to the transfer.
Yes, one of the advantages of FHA mortgages is that they are assumable. This can be a strong selling point if you decide to sell your home in the future.
